# The Hotels AP Automation Benchmark Report: Summer 2026 Edition


**by Mike Waldron**


## Why This Report Exists


Hotel finance runs on property-level accounting, where every invoice has to land in the right department, Rooms, F&B, Spa, and the right entity, before it ever reaches a consolidated GL. For a Controller managing AP across a multi-property portfolio, or a Regional Controller with visibility into a dozen properties at once, a misrouted invoice isn’t just an annoyance. It’s a department that’s miscoded its month, an aging report that doesn’t tell the truth, and a GM asking questions the Controller can’t yet answer.


Most operators know there’s leakage somewhere in their AP process. What they don’t have is the data to prove it: exactly how many duplicate invoices are slipping through, exactly how much exposure is sitting in flagged invoices, exactly how much faster the team could be closing if statement reconciliation wasn’t eating an hour per vendor per month. That gap between knowing something’s off and being able to point to it is where hotel AP has always struggled.


We process hundreds of thousands of invoices every quarter across our hotel customer base. This report is what that data actually shows, not industry estimates, not survey responses, but numbers pulled from real hotel operations.


This is the first edition. Twice a year, we’ll track how these numbers move, flag what’s driving the changes, and give hotel finance teams a benchmark they can actually use. This edition covers duplicate detection, fraud exposure, discrepancy rates, payment errors, invoice lifecycle time, and AP labor savings.


## Profitability Benchmarks


### Duplicate Detection


**Benchmark** : Hotel customers saved $471 million on 455,850 duplicate invoices flagged and prevented.


In the first half of 2026, hotel accounts caught 265,842 duplicates, preventing $293 million in overspending.


Duplicate values have risen every quarter, suggesting either that invoice values are climbing or that vendors are submitting higher-value duplicates. Either way, the trend makes automated detection increasingly critical, not optional, for multi-property operators processing this kind of volume.


### Invoice Risk


**Benchmark** : 89 percent of hotel customers had at least one invoice flagged for overcharges or fraud.


In the first half of 2026, 63 percent of hotel accounts had a flagged invoice, with the flagged invoices averaging $4,817 each.


Automated controls are dramatically outperforming manual processes at catching and preventing fraud before it escalates. For a Controller who used to find out about an overcharge during statement reconciliation, weeks after the fact, this is the difference between catching a problem and discovering one.


### Credit Recovery


**Benchmark:** Ottimate uncovered $488.1 million in credits related to refunds, adjustments, and overcharge corrections last year.


In the first half of 2026, Ottimate uncovered $358 million in credits related to refunds, adjustments and overcharges for hotels alone.


With continuous pricing increases, and invoice volumes on the rise, we continue to see the amount of overcharges increase. Implementing automation into your workflow is more important than ever to make sure you are catching these costly mistakes before they hit your bottom line.


### Payments


**Benchmark** : Ottimate caught 14,250 payments with errors last year, accounting for $1.6 million in potential losses.


So far this year, Ottimate has caught 6,026 payments with errors, accounting for $1.01 million in potential losses.


Payment errors are expensive and hard to recover once funds leave the account. Halfway through the year, hotel accounts are already closing in on last year’s full total. Manual payment reviews miss what automated checks catch consistently, which is exactly why a final validation layer before disbursement matters, whether payment runs through ACH or virtual card.


## Productivity Benchmarks


### Invoice Lifecycle Time


**Benchmark** : Hotel customers using Ottimate have reduced invoice lifecycle time from upload to approval from 11 days down to 5.3 days on average.


In the first half of 2026, hotel customers hit 3.14 days, 36 percent faster than the benchmark.


Hotel groups are continuing to accelerate even as invoice volume grows. For a property running month-end close on a tight calendar, that speed means fewer accruals to estimate and fewer surprises waiting in the aging report.


### AP Labor Savings


**Benchmark** : Ottimate saves hotel groups $69,000 per account per year in labor by reducing invoice lifecycle time, the equivalent of freeing up one full employee’s time for higher-value work.


In the first half of 2026, hotel accounts are saving 7.96 days per invoice compared to the manual baseline.


Hotel accounts are compounding efficiency gains as both speed improves and volume grows. That’s the time a Property Accountant or AP Manager gets back from statement reconciliation and exception handling, and time a Controller gets back for the work that actually requires judgment.


## About This Report


The Hotels AP Automation Benchmark Report: Summer 2026 Edition is published by Ottimate using aggregated, anonymized data from our hotel customer base. All benchmarks reflect real invoice processing data across independent properties, management companies, and multi-property hotel groups. This is the first edition; future editions will track trends and flag what’s driving the changes.
